reviewMethod: Visual review of each raw municipal panorama with the selected BAG wall and ground/ridge footprint projected through the shared camera model; the rectified strip was reviewed beside it.
note: Registration-reviewed, unlabelled development strips. Usable dispositions establish source-wall alignment for development, not opening ground truth, building identity, or citywide accuracy. Diagnostic-only cases must not enter opening metrics.

cases.focus: compound building whose selected BAG wall spans several visual facade segments
cases.review: Projection reaches the visible building, but the wall-to-architectural-unit correspondence is ambiguous.

cases.focus: traditional masonry beside modern infill with compound-footprint ambiguity
cases.review: Projection covers visually distinct construction within one BAG wall span; keep for ownership diagnosis only.

cases.focus: registered corner facade, repeated upper windows, commercial plinth and bicycle occlusion
cases.review: Projected wall edges follow the visible corner facade boundaries.

cases.focus: narrow irregular facade, staggered openings and severe foreground vehicle occlusion
cases.review: Wall registration is coherent; the vehicle makes this a useful partial-visibility case.

cases.focus: wide low industrial or garage frontage, large glazing and privacy blur
cases.review: Projected wall matches the complete wide frontage.

cases.focus: medium contemporary residential facade with large divided-light windows and a souterrain
cases.review: Both projected wall edges align with visible facade seams.

cases.focus: narrow canal facade with balconies, repeated windows and light branch occlusion
cases.review: Wall boundaries align with both neighbouring facade seams and openings remain measurable.

cases.focus: tall narrow facade with tree, market-stall and vehicle occlusion
cases.review: Projected wall matches the tall gabled unit; upper opening evidence remains usable.

cases.focus: wide restaurant shopfront, regular upper windows and stepped-gable termination
cases.review: Projected edges follow the visible architectural unit.

cases.focus: sparse contemporary cladding with few openings and a neighbouring gable intruding above
cases.review: Wall registration is exact; the sparse surface is retained to expose false opening proposals.

cases.focus: shopfront, entrance, paired upper windows and adjacent-building boundaries
cases.review: Projected wall edges isolate the red shopfront building.

cases.focus: monumental arched glazing, dense muntins, kiosk and lamp-post occlusion
cases.review: Projection isolates the intended church bay; treat it as a facade segment rather than the complete building.

rejectedPredecessors.reason: Rectification shows canal and street furniture instead of a usable target facade.
Distant facade is dominated by a tree and lacks usable opening evidence.
Extreme narrow crop contains one partial opening and no useful family context.
Projected wall falls in the alley or street beside the visible building.
Projected span crosses the road and several distant facades, so ownership is wrong.
Projected wall cuts through a corner building and a street gap.
Projected wall combines historic and modern neighbouring buildings.
A houseboat fully hides the selected facade plane.
Projected wall occupies the roadway and unrelated distant facades.
Projected wall cuts through a rounded compound footprint without matching architectural boundaries.
Target facade is too distant and hidden by parked cars and trees to support opening evidence.
